'''Nathalie Brigitte Anne Picqué''' (born December 2, 1973) is a French physicist. Picqué is the Director of the Precision Physics Division at the [[:de:Max-Born-Institut_für_Nichtlineare_Optik_und_Kurzzeitspektroskopie|Max Born Institute for Nonlinear Optics and Short Pulse Spectroscopy]]. She also holds a joint appointment in experimental physics Professor at [[Humboldt University of Berlin|HU Berlin]].

She is widely recognized for her pioneering work in developing broadband spectroscopy techniques using optical [[Frequency comb|frequency combs]]. These techniques including dual-comb spectroscopy and [[Fourier-transform spectroscopy]], have significantly pushed the limits of precision spectroscopy.

== Education and Career ==
Nathalie Picqué received<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/fellow_members/recent_fellows/2019_fellows/|title=Recent Fellows - Awards & Grants – The Optical Society (OSA) &#124; Optica}}</ref> a master's degree in laser physics from [[Paris-Sorbonne University]] and [[Ecole Polytechnique]], in [[Paris]], [[France]]. She went on to conduct her doctoral research at the [[Paris-Saclay University]] in [[Orsay]], [[France]] in [[Fourier-transform spectroscopy]], graduating in 1998. This was followed by a postdoctoral position at the [[European Laboratory for Non-Linear Spectroscopy]] in [[Florence]], [[Italy]], where she expanded on her doctoral work in frequency metrology and precision measurement with lasers. In 2001, she accepted a [[CNRS]] position and joined the  Laboratoire de Photophysique Moléculaire in Orsay (now [https://www.ismo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/accueil-ismo/ ISMO]).<ref>{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.photoniques.com/articles/photon/pdf/2024/05/photon2024128p21.pdf}}</ref>

In 2008, she moved to the [[Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics]] (MPQ) on a sabbatical, to work with the then-recent Nobel Laureate [[Theodor W. Hänsch]], on dual-combs spectroscopy. Eventually, she continued as a group leader at MPQ in [[Garching]] before moving to her current position at the Max Born Institute for Non Linear Optics and Short Pulse Spectroscopy.<ref>{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.optica.org/history/biographies/bios/nathalie_picque/}}</ref>

* 2010 Beller Lectureship Award <ref>{{Cite web| title=APS Beller Lectureship Recipients | url=https://www.aps.org/programs/international/programs/upload/ALL-Beller-Recipients.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100620003654/http://aps.org/programs/international/programs/upload/ALL-Beller-Recipients.pdf | archive-date=2010-06-20}}</ref>
* 2013 Coblentz Award <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.coblentz.org/awards/the-coblentz-award/|title=The Coblentz Award - Molecular Spectroscopy &#124; Coblentz Society}}</ref>
* 2019 Fellow of [[Optica (society)|Optica (formerly OSA)]]<ref name="auto"/>
* 2021 Gentner-Kastler Prize (German Physical Society, French Physical Society)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dpg-physik.de/auszeichnungen/dpg-preise-mit-anderen-organisationen/gentner-kastler-preis-und-medaille/preistraeger|title = Preisträgerinnen und Preisträger}}</ref>
* 2021 Advanced Grant (European Research Council) <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mpq.mpg.de/6711030/04-erc-advanced-grant-for-nathalie-picque |title = ERC Advanced Grant for Nathalie Picqué}}</ref>
* 2022 Helmholtz Prize (PTB) <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://idw-online.de/de/news792519|title = Helmholtz-Preis für zwei Optik-Gruppen mit Weltklasse}}</ref>
* 2022 [[Falling Walls]] Science Breakthrough in Physical Sciences <ref> {{Cite web|url=https://falling-walls.com/people/nathalie-picque/|title = Nathalie Picqué 2022 Science Breakthrough in Physical Sciences}} </ref>
* 2023: Grand Prix Cécile DeWitt-Morette / École de Physique des Houches of the French Academy of Sciences. <ref> {{Cite web|url= https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Laureats/laureate-2023-du-prix-cecile-dewitt-morette-ecole-de-physique-des-houches-cfm-fondation-pour-la-recherche-nathalie-picque.html |title = Nathalie Picqué 2023 Grand Prix Cécile DeWitt-Morette}}} </ref>
